body:
incident_bot: Pager: P1 — KV cache memory alarm on hosted-runtime cluster us-west-2-prod. High sustained growth in kv_cache_bytes, multiple OOM traces. API error rate 5xx rising ~8% in last 3m. Impact: generation endpoints (chat/completion) in hosted tier showing timeouts and 503s. Alert page: https://pager.example/incident/INC-6821 :rotating_light:

oncall_jess: I'm on it. Paging runtime oncall. First pass: check if continuous batching config was rolled in last 2 hours.

runtime_paul: seeing a surge in continuous-batching prefix lengths. Looks like a few customer requests with runaway context windows (>=250k tokens) are causing the KV store to keep huge KV entries. Eviction not kicking in fast enough.

sre_maya: can you paste the logs/stack traces? also metrics for kv_eviction_rate and batch_queue_length.

runtime_paul: grabbing slices. Relevant logs:```
[2026-03-15T10:02:13Z] host=rt-03 kv_store.go:412 WARN store_size_bytes=18446744073709551615 event=overflow candidate_key="session:usr_93a2"
[2026-03-15T10:02:16Z] host=rt-03 inference.go:872 ERR alloc failed: runtime: out of memory
[2026-03-15T10:02:18Z] host=rt-03 batcher.go:231 WARN continuous_batch length=1280 avg_tokens=8420
```
metrics snapshot (1m rollup): kv_cache_bytes=1.9TiB, kv_eviction_rate=0.2/sec, batch_size_p95=1220, host_mem_util=93%.

incident_bot: Auto-triage rule matched: "kv_cache_runaway_context_v2" (confidence high). Possible recent rollout: continuous-batching v3.1.4 applied to hosted pool ~+115m.

oncall_jess: hypothesis: continuous-batching change + an upstream customer sending massive context windows = cache blowup. Immediate aim: prevent further OOMs and remove persistent huge KV entries. Proposed mitigation steps (live):
1) Hotfix continuous-batcher to limit batch window length for hosted (temporarily) and disable unbounded prefix caching.
2) Increase eviction aggressiveness for entries > 4MB or > 50k tokens.
3) If necessary, roll back continuous-batching config to v3.1.3 for hosted pool.

sre_maya: agree. Also throttle new requests that have > 50k tokens at the reverse-proxy level so we stop accumulating more large KV state.

runtime_paul: applying step 1 now. Patching runtime config via control-plane API:```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/pools/us-west-2-prod/config \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"continuous_batching": {"max_prefix_tokens": 50000, "max_batch_window_ms": 100, "enabled": true}}'
```
Note: keeping enabled=true to preserve low-latency customers, but capping prefixes. Rolling to 5% canary then 100% if green.

oncall_jess: set canary to 5% and watch kv_cache_bytes.

support_alejandra: support is seeing ~12 distinct customer sessions with huge contexts; two customers have reported degraded responses manually (ticket IDs 34219, 34221). Notifying them that we're investigating.

pm_owen: flagging potential customer visible regression. Will draft a status update once we stabilize.

runtime_paul: canary patch applied to canary hosts (rt-canary-*) at 10:12Z. Early signals: kv_cache_bytes growth slope flattened on canaries. eviction_rate increased to 5/sec on canaries. No new OOMs in canary.

sre_maya: push to 100% after 5m if stable. Also prepare hotfix script to directly evict top N largest KV entries across nodes (controlled evictions).

runtime_paul: running eviction script (dry-run first):```bash
# list largest kv entries > 10MB
redis-cli -h rt-cache --bigkeys | awk '/largest/ {print $0}' | head -n 20
# targeted eviction
for k in $(./list-large-keys.sh --min-bytes 10485760); do redis-cli -h rt-cache del "$k"; done
```
Dry run shows ~36 sessions exceed 10MB; will evict oldest first.

oncall_jess: Hold evictions until we confirm customer impact. support_alejandra to confirm owners for those sessions.

support_alejandra: confirming owners now, 18 sessions are from internal test orgs / bots; safe to evict. 18 sessions mapped to paying customers -> need approval from pm_owen for evict.

pm_owen: approve eviction for internal/test org keys and for any sessions older than 24h. For active paying customers, coordinate with customer_ops before eviction.

incident_bot: Scheduled live actions: disable_unbounded_prefix_cache (canary 10:12Z), cap_prefix_tokens=50k (applied), targeted_evictions (manual, pending approvals).

runtime_paul: pushing the rollback plan in parallel in case canary fails. Rollback command:```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/pools/us-west-2-prod/rollback \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' \n  -d '{"to_version": "v3.1.3"}'
```

oncall_jess: monitoring panels: kv_cache_bytes, kv_eviction_rate, batch_size_p95, host_mem_util, request_5xx_rate, per-customer-queue-length. Setting Slack alert if any of these exceed thresholds.

sre_maya: after canary -> full rollout at 10:20Z. Metrics show decline: kv_cache_bytes from 1.9TiB -> 1.35TiB in 12m. Error rate down to 1.2%. No new OOMs for 18m.

support_alejandra: informed customers: temporary mitigation applied, risk of truncated sessions for very long contexts; proactively opening support threads for affected paid customers.

pm_owen: logging action items: 1) Postmortem + RCA, 2) Add guardrails in control plane to prevent applying continuous-batching config without prefix caps to hosted pools, 3) Per-tenant kv caps (soft limits + backpressure), 4) Improve eviction policy to consider token counts not just size.

oncall_jess: handing off to next oncall @runtime_paul_night in 30m. Current status: stable under mitigations, canary->100% rolled. Recommend follow-up: run deep scan for orphaned sessions, backfill metrics for token counts per session.

customer_ops: please coordinate customer communication for the two paying customers we flagged. Provide timeline and remediation steps.

incident_bot: Incident severity reduced to P2 at 10:45Z; automated monitoring will alert if regressions reappear. Incident owner: oncall_jess. Postmortem owner: pm_owen.

oncall_jess: short notes for postmortem: timeline, root cause (continuous-batching change + unbounded prefix caching + large customer contexts), mitigations (prefix caps, eviction, proxy throttling), long-term fixes.

sre_maya: saving traces and heap dumps to //artifacts/incidents/INC-6821/ for follow-up.

runtime_paul: final command we used to throttle at the proxy layer:```nginx
# rate limit requests with large content-length header
map $http_content_length $large_body {
  default 0;
  ~^[5-9][0-9]{4,} 1;
}
limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=large_body:10m rate=1r/s;
server {
  if ($large_body) {
    limit_req zone=large_body burst=2 nodelay;
  }
}
```

oncall_jess: thanks all. Leaving notes in incident channel and creating the incident doc. Passing to night oncall. :white_check_mark:

support_alejandra: adding ticket links to incident doc and emailing customers.

pm_owen: will pick up postmortem. Good work getting this under control.
